newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-ENQVIST GIVES SWEDEN CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST GIVES SWEDEN CUP LEAD.

text.p: Swedish number one Thomas Enqvist gave his country a 1-0 lead in a Davis Cup world group quarter-final tie against South Africa on Friday by beating Grant Stafford in four sets.
After they split the first two sets, Enqvist took control in the third and cantered to victory 7-5 2-6 6-4 6-1.
"I knew it would be a tough match. He is a dangerous player," Enqvist said after the match of nearly three hours in the southern town of Vaxjo, about 400 kms south of Stockholm.
"He has a different style from others because he is trying to come in on every serve and he tried to put pressure on me. I was on the defence all the time."

Jonas Bjorkman was facing South Africa's top player, Wayne Ferreira, in the second singles. Saturday's doubles pits Bjorkman and Nicklas Kulti against David Adams and Ellis Ferreira, with the two reverse singles on Sunday.
Stafford, world-ranked 69th, did well with his strong backhand and good placements as he gave the world number seven a real battle in the first two sets.
Ranked 282nd early in 1996, Stafford broke Enqvist's serve in the seventh game of the first set but the Swede broke back in the 10th and broke again in the 12th.
The second set went to the 25-year-old South African but the match turned Enqvist's way when he came back from two break points in the third game of the third set.
"I was struggling in the second set," Enqvist, 23, said. "But in the third and fourth sets I think I served much better than in the first two sets ... I found my rhythm again."
It is the seventh time Sweden and South Africa have met in the Davis Cup, the Swedes having won five times.
